item.title: Josh Hokit offers to save ‘bum’ UFC light heavyweight division, Navajo Stirling responds
item.description: Josh Hokit weighs in at UFC 334 | Jeff Bottari, Zuffa LLC Josh Hokit has brought plenty of excitement to the heavyweight division, now he might drop down in weight and do the same. If that’s what Hokit decides to do, top contender Navajo Stirling will be waiting for him. The undefeated Stirling currently finds himself in an awkward position, having scored consecutive knockouts over former light heavyweight champions Jiri Prochazka and Jan Blachowicz to make a compelling No. 1 contender case. One huge problem: The current champion of the division is Stirling’s friend and teammate Carlos Ulberg, and their coach Eugene Bareman has made it clear a bout between the two is out of the question. Hokit responded to Bareman’s comments on social media, writing, “I need to save this bum division as well. If you need a guy, you know who to call.” Stirling was quick to respond, “Book it then,” tagging the UFC and Dana White. View this post on Instagram Hokit is fresh off of a defeat to heavyweight champion Ciryl Gane in the UFC 334 main event. Despite giving Gane all he could handle for five rounds, Gane went on to earn the unanimous decision nod. Since then, Hokit has campaigned for a rematch, but given that he’s on the lighter end of the scale compared to the rest of the heavyweight roster, it’s not out of the realm of possibility that he attempts to become a contender at 205 pounds instead in the near future. The UFC likely waiting for other dominoes to fall in the two divisions before making any decisions, with the popular Alex Pereira attempting to earn another heavyweight title shot when he fights Sergei Pavlovich at UFC 335 on Dec. 12, return dates still unclear for Ulberg and former heavyweight champion Tom Aspinall, and top light heavyweight contender Magomed Ankalaev also waiting in the wings.

item.title: Alan Smith expects Arsenal to sell struggling star in January
item.description: Alan Smith expects Arsenal to sell struggling star in January Alan Smith has joined the debate over Arsenal’s potential January transfer business, and he believes the Gunners should have no problem selling Viktor Gyokeres if doing so would help them bring in another striker. The Swedish forward remains an important member of the Arsenal squad, but he has struggled to establish himself as a regular starter. Kai Havertz continues to be preferred in the role despite not scoring consistently, leaving Gyokeres struggling to secure a more prominent position. Arsenal signed Gyokeres after he established himself as one of Europe’s most prolific strikers , but his performances at the Emirates have not matched those expectations. He has struggled to make the desired impact and has arguably performed below the level he showed last season. With the Gunners potentially looking to invest in new players during the January transfer window, selling members of the current squad could help fund those moves. Smith believes Gyokeres is a player Arsenal could afford to let go if the right opportunity arises. Smith backs potential Gyokeres sale The former Arsenal striker does not believe selling Gyokeres would necessarily be a mistake, particularly if the money received could help the club recruit another forward. He also feels the Swedish international would attract interest from other clubs because of the qualities he has demonstrated. Smith believes Gyokeres could perform better in a different system, where his strengths might be used more effectively. Speaking via the Metro , he explained: ‘Well, if it meant they could get somebody else in, I think you would. ‘He’s still a very sellable striker, I think. Other clubs would look at him and think he would fit into our style of play in a way that perhaps he doesn’t with Arsenal. And he showed with that goal last night that he’s still got something to offer. But on a consistent basis, it’s not been working for Arsenal.’ (Photo by Mike Hewitt/Getty Images) Arsenal face decision over their striker options Smith’s comments highlight the uncertainty surrounding Gyokeres’ future at the Emirates . Although the striker has shown that he still has something to offer, his performances have not convinced everyone that he is the right long-term option for Arsenal. The Gunners may have to consider whether keeping him or selling him to fund another signing would better serve their ambitions. If they decide to strengthen their attack, Gyokeres could become one of the players whose future needs to be assessed. For now, the striker still has an opportunity to improve his standing in the squad, but Smith believes Arsenal should remain open to selling him if it helps bring in a better-fitting alternative. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ ADMIN COMMENT So here are some simple rules which I must insist commenters follow…. item.title: Sunderland held by Polish side Jagiellonia
item.description: UEFA Europa League Sunderland 1 - 1 Jagiellonia Białystok FT Sunderland are still to play AC Milan and Anderlecht away in the league phase [Getty Images] Sunderland's struggles returned as they were held to a frustrating draw by Polish side Jagiellonia Bialystok at home in the Europa League. Timur Tutierov opened the scoring for the hosts in the 47th minute by heading in Enzo Le Fee's deflected cross from a yard out. Jagiellonia, who are ninth in the Polish first division, equalised five minutes later when Kamil Jozwiak intercepted Reinildo Mandava's poor back pass and tapped in after rounding Sunderland goalkeeper Robin Roefs. Jagiellonia arguably had the better chances to win the game with Roefs doing particularly well to keep out Jozwiak with a diving save when the former Derby forward capitalised on Jules Ahoka's sloppy pass. Sunderland, who are 18th in the Premier League, have now won just two of their past eight games and in the Europa League have collected eight points from their five matches. Last season 10 points were needed to guarantee progression to the knockouts and the season before 11 points was the crucial total. item.title: Dodgers sign Eric Wagaman to minor-league deal
item.description: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - AUGUST 25: First baseman Eric Wagaman #39 of the New York Mets stands in the batting box while playing the Milwaukee Brewers at Citi Field on August 25, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Benjamin B. Braun/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Dodgers are making moves this Thanksgiving, as they signed infielder Eric Wagaman to a minor-league contract with an invitation to spring training on Wednesday. He was subsequently reassigned to Triple-A Oklahoma City on Thursday. Francys Romero of Beisbolfr.com was the first to report the signing. After dealing for Minnesota Twins infielder Royce Lewis last week, the Dodgers add another potential right-handed platoon option that has spent time at first base, third base and left field at the big league level. Wagaman has spent parts of three seasons with the Angels, Miami Marlins and New York Mets and across 184 games, he has combined to slash .245/.291/.376 with 11 home runs and 60 RBI, posting a wRC+ of 86 and -0.6 fWAR. Wagaman began the 2026 calendar year with Miami, but he was traded to the Minnesota Twins on Jan. 2 for left-handed pitcher Kade Bragg. Wagaman was optioned to Triple-A St. Paul on March 23 and he was designated for assignment by Minnesota on April 23. He was claimed off waivers by the Mets four days later, and he bounced around between the big league club and Triple-A Syracuse. Wagaman tallied just 52 plate appearances across 26 games at the highest level, slashing .191/.269/.319 with two home runs and five RBI. In 55 Triple-A games with St. Paul and Syracuse, he slashed .244/.333/.389 with five home runs and 30 RBI across 222 plate appearances. Wagaman will have to compete with the likes of Lewis and Alex Freeland should the Dodgers need a supplemental right-handed platoon bat at the corner infield positions, but he has proven to be a viable option against left-handers at the big league level. In 124 games against left-handed pitching, Wagaman is slashing .262/.306/.424 with seven home runs, 31 RBI and 14 doubles over 245 plate appearances.

Cristiano Ronaldo , already owning the record for most goals for club and country in the sport's long and storied history, is getting closer to scoring for the 1,000th time in his senior career. Having turned 41 years old in February 2026, Ronaldo faces a race against time — and the decline of his own physical capabilities — to reach this milestone. Should he successfully accomplish it, however, it would be an epic triumph of fitness, talent, longevity, and dominance that would ring throughout football's past and present, as well as long into the future. item.description: ILLUSTRATION - A view of the NFL logo on the pitch before the 2026 NFL Game between Atalanta Falcons and Cincinnati Bengals at the Santiago Bernabeu. (is associated with: «Bears complete sensational comeback to beat Lions on Thanksgiving») Nathalia Araújo/dpa The Chicago Bears completed a sensational comeback and scored a last-gasp touchdown to beat the Detroit Lions 39-35 in their divisional clash on Thanksgiving Thursday. The Lions led throughout the close and entertaining game and had an 11-point lead halfway through the fourth quarter, thanks to Jahmyr Gibbs 70-yard run for a touchdown. But the Bears hit back in their following possession and had the ball again with some two minutes on the clock. item.title: Lyman Hall football holds off determined Sheehan team to snap 13-game losing strerak in Carini Bowl
item.description: Lyman Hall senior quarterback Ryan Casey threw for 101 yards and two touchdowns, and also ran for 145 yards and a touchdown as Sheehan clinched the third seed in the CIAC Class M playoffs and snapped a 13-game losing streak in the Carini Bowl with a 28-20 win over Sheehan on Thursday, Nov. 26, 2026. (Mike Madera/For Hearst Connecticut Media) WALLINGFORD – Over the last 13 games between the city rivals, the Lyman Hall football team has seen the Sheehan Titans celebrate. The script finally flipped. Jumping out to an early 20-point lead, the Trojans held on to defeat Sheehan 28-20 in the 54th Carini Bowl at Riccitelli Field at Sheehan High School Thursday morning. With the victory, Lyman Hall not only unofficially clinched the third seed and a home game in Class M, but the Trojans evened the Carini Bowl series at 27, snapping Sheehan's 13-game win streak in the series. "It's special," Lyman Hall coach C.J. Monroe said after his team improved to 8-2 and clinched the first postseason home game in program history. "There's been, five years ago, people doubting it and saying that this could never be done. For this group to host the first ever home football game at Lyman Hall, I'm so proud of this community, this team, and I'm sure Tuesday night, the crowd will be rocking." Leading 20-7 at the half, Lyman Hall capped a 9-play, 57-yard drive to start the second half with an 8-yard touchdown run by quarterback Ryan Casey. Casey then hit Brandon LaPlante for the 2-point conversion and a 28-7 Lyman Hall lead 5 minutes, 36 seconds into the third quarter. "I'm so proud of my team," Casey said after rushing for 145 yards and a touchdown. "They played amazing. Defensively, would have liked to stop the run a little bit better. They've got some tough guys over there. The turnovers on our end kept them in it. We got the win. The trophy is coming home." Sheehan, which was in the uncharacteristic spot of not playing for a playoff spot or seed, refused to back down and responded with a 5-play, 70-yard drive, ending with a 27-yard score by Zack O'Brien to get within 28-14 with 4:02 left in the third quarter. The Sheehan defense then took over with an interception by Isaiah Forbs, and a fumble recovery by O'Brien. The Titans followed O'Brien's fumble recovery with an 8-play, 48-yard drive which saw quarterback Tyler Costanzo hit Sebastian Rosario with a 5-yard touchdown pass on fourth down to get within 28-20 with 2:56 remaining in the fourth quarter. "We had a couple of mental mistakes, a couple of breakdowns that resulted in some big plays for them early," Sheehan coach John Ferrazzi said after his team completed the season at 4-6. "I was just proud of our guys, being down 20-0 against a team with an explosive offense like that. We were able to settle in and make it a ball game. We had a chance there." Any chance of a Sheehan comeback disappeared when Casey ran the ball four times, picking up two first downs to help run out the clock and clinch Lyman Hall's first win

item.title: Leeds United Fend Off Man United For England Star: Is 2029 Wise?
item.description: Leeds United Fend Off Man United For England Star: Is 2029 Wise? Leeds United have agreed terms with striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin on a new contract until 2029, according to The Athletic , with the deal carrying a club-record wage. The agreement fends off January interest from Manchester United and removes the risk of the 29-year-old leaving on a free transfer in 2028. An England recall this month shows why Leeds acted early. What Calvert-Lewin has given Leeds Calvert-Lewin arrived from Everton on a free transfer in August 2025, with fitness the main worry after he managed three league goals in 26 appearances the previous season. Since then he has missed just three of 49 league games and scored 18 goals in 46 Premier League appearances. This season he has five goals in 956 minutes from 11 starts, and his expected goals of 5.77 suggest the finishing is matching the chances. One of those was a penalty, and he scored and set up another in the 4-1 win at Chelsea on 21 November. Strengths and weaknesses on the pitch Calvert-Lewin attacks crosses and finishes with few touches, and 13 of his 25 shots this season have hit the target. His limits are just as visible. He wins 48.9 per cent of his aerial duels, an ordinary return for a target man, and one assist in 11 starts shows he creates little for others. Leeds are also finalising a one-year extension until 2028 for understudy Lukas Nmecha, who has scored six goals in 1,288 minutes. That is a goal roughly every 215 minutes, a respectable return for a backup striker. Is this the right call for Leeds United? LONDON, ENGLAND – NOVEMBER 21: Dominic Calvert-Lewin of Leeds United scores the 1st Leeds United goal during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Chelsea FC and Leeds United at Stamford Bridge on November 21, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images) Yes, though the length of the contract deserves more scrutiny than the wage. Replacing a striker with 18 goals in 46 league games would cost Leeds a fee plus wages, and that output rarely comes cheap. Transfermarkt values Calvert-Lewin at around £19m , and Leeds signed him for nothing, so securing him is straightforward economics. Losing him to Manchester United would hand a Premier League rival a proven goalscorer and leave Daniel Farke with little time to recruit a replacement. The risk sits in 2029. He will be 32 when the deal ends, and a record wage for a player who relies on movement and physical duels leaves little margin for decline. His injury record at Everton makes that concern real, even though he has stayed fit since arriving. Nmecha covers the short term adequately, but neither striker adds much creativity, so a younger forward arriving by next summer would protect the squad better than another extension.

item.title: Jack Miller to revive unraced Australian GP livery for MotoGP farewell
item.description: Motorsport photo Jack Miller will contest this weekend’s MotoGP finale in Valencia in a special livery that he was originally due to run at his final Australian Grand Prix appearance last month. The 31-year-old will carry Australia’s national sporting colours on his Pramac Yamaha bike on Sunday, as he brings the curtain down on his 12-year stint in the premier class. The Townsville-born rider had previously unveiled the striking gold-and-blue colour scheme at Phillip Island last month, pairing it with a matching leather suit. However, with the Australian Grand Prix subsequently getting cancelled due to poor visibility, Miller never had the opportunity to race in the livery. The four-time grand prix winner had previously hinted at the possibility of reviving the livery, and confirmed ahead of the Valencia weekend that he would also wear a special helmet commemorating his MotoGP career. “Yeah, I’ve got the Phillip Island livery on Sunday, but I got a really, really, really special helmet for Sunday as well. You'll see more of that to come but it's something I'm extremely proud of,” Miller said on Thursday at Valencia. Jack Miller, Pramac Racing Jack Miller, Pramac Racing Miller made his MotoGP debut in 2015 as part of Honda’s satellite structure, before scoring his maiden victory at the Dutch GP the following year. He moved to Pramac in 2018 and earned a promotion to Ducati's factory team alongside Francesco Bagnaia . After winning three races on the Desmosedici, Miller moved to KTM in 2023 but struggled to replicate his previous results on the RC16. He was limited by the competitiveness of the machinery during his final two seasons in MotoGP with Pramac, but his technical knowledge and relationship with Yamaha continues with a factory contract in WorldSBK for 2027. Asked what he was most proud of during his time in MotoGP, Miller said: “I think being able to adapt to any situation, whether it's wet, dry, new bike, old bike, whatever, within a day - not even within a day, within a session I'm where I need to be. I'm able to adapt to everything very quickly. item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect While his name doesn’t always come up on the broadcast or on the scoresheet, Marco Kasper has been a big piece for the Red Wings since coming back from an upper body injury that derailed the start of his season. The third year forward has been quietly digging in on the forecheck or carrying the puck into the offensive zone for the team, and even though Detroit hasn’t always been able to capitalize on those chances of late, his coaches are liking what they’re seeing. “You know, and I couldn’t even tell you how many goals or assists he has. Which is probably a good thing. Last year at this time, we’re going, well, when’s he going to score again?” Head coach Todd McLellan said, “He looks like he’s enjoying the game. I’m happy for him.” Making his mark For the record, Kasper has a goal and two assists in his last five games. Modest production, certainly, but below the surface, his advanced statistics tell the real story. Kasper has an expected goals for percentage of 57.84%, and actual goals for percentage of 66.67% according to Statpede , which means he’s got a little bit of luck on his side as the shots and attempts he has on net are bouncing the right way, going in a little more than the outlet’s model would usually predict. More importantly, Kasper has been driving play into those high danger areas for his teammates. “I don’t think he gets enough recognition, because he does a lot of the dirty work. Getting to the net, the heavy work along the boards, keeping plays alive.” McLellan said. For the last couple of games Kasper has been playing with Viktor Arvidsson and Emmitt Finnie , two of the Red Wings most productive forwards so far this year. McLellan had originally had the trio together to start the year in training camp, however, injuries and the need to bump Finnie up to the team’s first line center split the three up until recently. After a 7-game drought, Emmitt Finnie posts points for the second game in a row. Needing more Still, the Red Wings need more, from not only Kasper, but the rest of the lineup as well. Before the game against the Canucks, Arvidsson had been scoreless for nearly a month. item.description: Real Madrid open to winter offers for two players The board at La Liga giants Real Madrid are ready to negotiate the sales of a pair of first-team players, in the case of sufficient offers arriving this winter. This comes amid the understanding that Los Blancos are open to the potential departures of both Ferland Mendy and Raúl Asencio. Owing to respective injury problems, in fact, neither player has taken to the pitch on a single occasion in Real Madrid’s colours. item.description: (Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images) DETROIT — It never felt like Bears quarterback Caleb Williams settled in against the Detroit Lions’ defense. Until he did. Williams finished 30-for-44 passing for 345 yards, with two fourth-quarter touchdowns to receiver Rome Odunze , including the game-winner with three seconds left in the game. He was also sacked four times for 33 yards, including one costly strip-sack that resulted in a safety in the final two minutes of the first half. Tight end Colston Loveland was carted to the locker room after he was rolled up on in the first quarter of the Bears’ 39-35 win on Thanksgiving Day . The Bears’ run game took a massive step forward, too, scoring three times and gaining xxx yards on the ground. Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs torched the Bears defense for 146 yards on 24 carries. His third rushing touchdown of the game went for 70 yards against a gassed Bears defense. But it wasn’t enough to down the Cardiac Bears. The CHGO staff reacts to the Bears’ win … Adam Hoge : What in the world did we just watch?!? Iceman did it again. And Rome Odunze is forever forgiven for any previous end zone drops. The Bears didn’t take the lead until the final three seconds. Caleb Williams, Rome Odunze and T.J. Edwards were all heroes in this one. But here’s the big takeaway: the Bears are a legitimate Super Bowl contender. No doubt about it now. For Bears and Lions fans situated on their couches, it was a stressful start to Thanksgiving Day. The Bears deserve all the credit in the world for pulling that one out. It felt like one they had no business winning, but they never fell too far behind. What a return for the Cardiac Bears. Greg Braggs Jr. : Iceman, cometh. item.title: Police response to Besiktas fans' pro-Palestine banner 'unacceptable'
item.description: UEFA Europa League Beşiktaş 2 - 1 Hapoel Be'er Sheva FT Besiktas fans unfurled a pro-Palestinian banner during their Europa League match against Israeli side Hapoel Be'er-Sheva in Georgia [Getty Images] The Turkish Football Federation has strongly condemned the "unacceptable" actions of Georgian police towards Besiktas fans who unfurled a pro-Palestinian banner during their Europa League match against Israeli side Hapoel Be'er-Sheva. Besiktas say they have lodged a complaint with European football's governing body Uefa over "disproportionate" use of force by Georgian police. The match was moved from Istanbul to Batumi, Georgia for safety and security reasons but had to be suspended in the 25th minute after clashes involving Besiktas supporters and local police. Both the officiating team and the Besiktas players left the field, but play was able to resume 30 minutes later. "We strongly condemn the unacceptable attitudes, behaviour and actions directed at Besiktas supporters inside and outside the stadium before and during the Uefa Europa League match between our representative Besiktas and Hapoel Be'er-Sheva," a statement from the Turkish federation read. Turkish outlet NTV reported that Georgian police had gone into the stands and used pepper spray on the Besiktas fans. The report added that there were anti-Israeli chants from the Turkish fans and that Besiktas players and director of football Onder Ozen spoke to supporters to try to calm matters before play restarted. Hakan Fidan, Turkey's minister of foreign affairs, spoke to his Georgian counterpart Maka Botchorishvili following the incident. "Officials from the Turkish embassy in Tbilisi and the Consulate General in Batumi are at the stadium," a Turkish foreign ministry source said. "All necessary steps are being taken to ensure the safety of our citizens and protect their rights." Besiktas won the match 2-1. Ten-man Bournemouth beat Celta for 10th win in row

item.title: Ndamukong Suh names whether Aaron Rodgers or Antonio Brown handled their NFL release worse
item.description: Credit: Elsa/Cliff Welch/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Former NFL star Ndamukong Suh has presented his view on Aaron Rodgers’ actions after being released by the Pittsburgh Steelers. Former Lions and Buccaneers star Ndamukong Suh says he believed Aaron Rodgers handled his release from the Steelers wrongly. Rodgers was benched by the team, and responded by going on the Pat McAfee Show to call out head coach Mike McCarthy, and vowing never to play for the Steelers again. He was cut around an hour later. Speaking to Sky Sports UK, Ndamukong Suh says the Steelers and Aaron Rodgers could have handled the situation better by coming to a better agreement behind the scenes and working out their differences. But he reserved most of his criticism for Rodgers, saying that airing his grievances on a national show is not the right way to go about his business. Suh said: “There’s a way you go about handling those things, and I think there’s a way on both sides of the ball, from McCarthy’s side and the organization side, but also from Aaron Rodgers’ side of how you handle that. “And those things should be handled behind closed doors before trying to get ahead of the story on either side of the ball. Let’s have a conversation. Let’s have an understanding, and then we can go from there and address. “Going out to the media and running and doing all these different things, the McAfee show, which is great for them and great for ESPN, but ultimately that to me is not the proper way I would want to handle something in that particular scenario.” Suh says Antonio Brown handled situation better Ndamukong Suh was part of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers team with Antonio Brown, when the star wide receiver walked off the field against the Jets. Suh says that despite the situation being obvious that Brown’s career in Tampa Bay was over, the franchise and even the wide receiver handled the situation properly. He said: “There was a way the organization handled that, and yes, everybody knew who was going to get released. “Did he handle it the right way? item.title: Levski Sofia coach says Marseille fan clashes 'unacceptable' as five hospitalised
item.description: A blood-stained Levski Sofia supporter tries to escape from Marseille supporters ahead of the Europa League match (Justine MEDDAH) Levski Sofia coach Julio Velazquez said violent fan clashes ahead of their Europa League game at Marseille on Thursday, which resulted in five supporters of the Bulgarian club being taken to hospital, were "unacceptable for football". The lead-up to the match at the Stade Velodrome was marred by incidents in the stands between the two sets of supporters, including the throwing of projectiles and flares. Several Marseille fans ran from the stand where they were situated about 10 minutes before kick-off, appearing to pursue a group of Bulgarian supporters. They breached the stand designated for away fans, where around 500 Levski supporters were gathered. "Five people were taken to hospital with eye injuries, head trauma and a dislocated shoulder," the Marseille police prefecture told AFP. "Six others were treated on site for various wounds." The police source said all the people injured were Bulgarian and there was "no information at this stage regarding any arrests". Security personnel eventually managed to restore calm as the game kicked off on time. "It's a very regrettable episode -- these are incidents which are unacceptable for football," said Velazquez. "I support the fans who were caught up in this incident. I hope nothing serious has happened. I'm very saddened by this situation." Ligue 1 club Marseille said it was "working to understand the precise circumstances of these incidents". There were a few further flare-ups between the fans, notably during the half-time break. "We are living through violent times in our society, so this is very, very regrettable," said Marseille coach Bruno Genesio. The home team went on to win the game 1-0. stt/jc/nf

item.title: Tyson Fury never received schizophrenia diagnosis, wife Paris confirms
item.description: The British Boxing Board of Control will assess Tyson Fury ahead of his hotly anticipated bout against Anthony Joshua following comments he made about hearing voices during a mental health episode, although earlier suggestions that he had received a schizophrenia diagnosis have since been refuted. A new self-titled documentary about the 38-year-old, to be released on Netflix on Friday, goes into detail about his past mental health struggles. He and his wife Paris recalled frightening episodes in which he heard voices threatening him and his family after he was hospitalised with a suspected heart attack in 2016. He said: “Words can’t explain the darkness I was in. It was like the living version of the pits of hell’s fire. I 100 per cent thought I’d end up in a padded room with the door locked and that scared me so much.” In the original version of the documentary, which has since been edited before release, Paris said he was “mild schizophrenic”, but it was confirmed on Thursday that he was not medically diagnosed. Doctors said he had experienced a severe anxiety attack. Paris clarified her comments on Thursday, saying: “I want to clarify a statement I made in the original version of the Tyson Fury documentary. I recalled a conversation from many years ago when discussing Tyson’s condition and I used the word ‘schizophrenic’. “Whilst Tyson did show some symptoms associated with schizophrenia, he doesn’t have this condition and has never received a diagnosis. Mental health is complex, and it isn't always easy to find the right words, especially when you're living it with someone you love. I’m so proud of Tyson for really opening up in this documentary and want to say thank you for all the support we’ve received as a family.” A Netflix spokesperson said: “Following new information shared by the family relating to Tyson’s official mental health diagnosis, we have worked alongside them to update the documentary accordingly ahead of launch.” In comments made before the documentary was updated, the British Boxing Board of Control said it would evaluate Fury’s fitness to box Joshua, with the fight scheduled for 11 December in Cardiff’s Principality Stadium . The board’s general secretary, Robert Smith, told BBC Sport : “We are in the process of dealing with the matter but if there are any medical issues we wouldn't let anyone box, doesn't matter if it's Tyson Fury or not, it could be anybody. “I'm fairly confident he will be absolutely fine. We're dealing with it now and we'll have an answer very shortly. “If our doctors are satisfied he's fit to box, he will box.” He declined to comment on the specifics of the process, saying, “it's a medical matter”.

item.title: Curley Cup tradition ends after 63 games with an Audubon win
item.description: AUDUBON — Paul Frantz looked sadly at the soggy field minutes before kickoff. For much of his life, Frantz has spent Thanksgiving at either Audubon or Haddon Township High School. Yet Thursday was the final time he would spend the holiday at either school. It was earlier announced that this was to be the last game the two schools would play on Thanksgiving. They will still compete, but due to the ever-changing playoff system, where a team could end its regular season well before Halloween, Thanksgiving football is going the way of the dinosaur. There were only seven games scheduled for either Thanksgiving, or the night before this year in South Jersey. (Two got postponed to Friday and Saturday, due to the inclement weather). After Audubon’s 29-0 win over Haddon Township, this is another rivalry that will be staged on another day. In fact, the two schools will play Nov. 11 on Veterans Day next year at Haddon Township. The series began in 1963, but according to South Jersey historian Chuck Langerman, the two schools started playing on Thanksgiving in 1965. Audubon has now won 14 in a row and increased its series lead to 45-17-1. For Frantz, Thanksgiving football, especially between these two rivals, meant everything. He is a 1968 graduate of Audubon and later was an assistant coach at Haddon Township and a head coach at Audubon. “I have been coming to this game since I was 10-years-old,” said Frantz, who was a second-team All-South Jersey receiver during his playing days at Audubon. “I knew people who would fly in to attend this game, and I am not happy to see this tradition end.” There are many others in his corner, but unfortunately, many of them decided to sit this one out. The inclement weather kept the crowd at a minimum. One tradition will continue — the awarding of the Curley Cup to the winning team. This is named for the late Tom Curley, who earned distinction as a head coach at both Audubon and Haddon Township. According to Langerman, Curley succeeded former Eagles general manager Harry Gamble as head coach at Audubon and went 58-36-4 from 1962 to 1972. He then moved on to Haddon Township where he went 56-46-4 from 1973 to 1983. On that final 1983 team was a defensive end named Pat Curley, who happens to be Tom’s son. Pat Curley presented the Curley Cup to the winning Audubon team. “It’s sad that this is ending on Thanksgiving,” Pat Curley said. “I grew up with five sisters and our lives revolved around the game on Thanksgiving, all eight of us, that is where our lives were.” The order was clearly set — morning football and then afternoon Thanksgiving dinner. “The game was the main focus either when my father was at Audubon or Haddon Township,” Pat Curley said. “And it’s sad that it’s ending the tradition, the way it is, but I understand it is the reality of today’s world.” Haddon Township athletic director Tim George says this was a move that he thought had to be made. item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. Vanney still has two years left on his lucrative contract while Kuntz’s deal ends next month, so if there’s going to be a fall guy for the Galaxy’s recent failures, it’s likely to be the GM, not the coach. On Friday, Kuntz was already speaking of the team in the past tense. “I really enjoyed my time at the Galaxy. I love being here,” he said. “I’d like to be back if it was up to me. But it’s not.” Nor is it up to the team’s most loyal supporters, who would like to see someone sacrificed for the team’s fall from grace. item.title: Cavan Sullivan named MLS Young Player of the Year 🌟
item.description: Cavan Sullivan named MLS Young Player of the Year 🌟 Philadelphia Union and USMNT midfielder Cavan Sullivan has capped a record-setting regular season by being named the 2026 MLS Young Player of the Year. In his first full campaign, the Man City-bound starlet emerged as one of the league's most exciting young talents, finishing with with a career-high 23 goal contributions (nine goals, 14 assists) in 29 appearances, and recorded a goal contribution in 10 consecutive matches, the longest such run by a teenager in MLS history. Both his total of 23 goal contributions and his 14 assists are the most ever by a teenager in a single MLS season. Sullivan's form also earned him MLS Player of the Month honors for September 2026. At 17 years and two days old, he became the youngest winner of the award in league history. His production on the club level soon translated to the international stage. Sullivan received his first call-up to the US men's national team in September and made his debut against Peru, becoming the second-youngest player in USMNT history to start a match. He has since collected four senior caps and added another milestone to his résumé by scoring against Mexico at 17 years and five days old, making him the youngest goalscorer in USMNT history.

item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. Tall turned to a scouting network led by Mark Nichols, bringing in a proven MLS veteran in Santi Rodriguez, Chile national team forward Gonzalo Tapia, securing a loan deal for Moroccan winger Anass Zaroury and signing designated player Brais Mendez, a Spanish attacker whose arrival from Real Sociedad brought to mind that of Cucho Hernandez. While Mendez is at a different stage of his carer than Hernandez was, he turned into a star in Columbus, showing his full potential in MLS after frustrating stints with Watford and loans in Huseca, Mallorca and Getafe. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images “I think that’s also part of the sadness,” head coach Juan Carlos Amorós said. “I think we never know what would have happened if we played on a good pitch. I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable.” Tickets for the semifinal were reallotted and grabbed up in a hurry, while Gotham officials ground on the logistics of moving their game-day operations. “Obviously not ideal we had to change stadiums, but … I think that’s really awesome to come into a new environment, a new stadium, you have to adapt, you have to make sure you can bring that energy and our supporters did that tonight and that’s incredible,” Gotham midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Gotham FC’s home semifinal moved to 5K-seat stadium in field quality debacle
item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. Providing our players with a high-quality surface to compete is a responsibility we take very seriously.” The Gotham FC starting eleven line up before the NWSL playoff quarterfinal in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Lev Radin/Shutterstock Gotham is a tenant of Major League Soccer’s Red Bull New York at Sports Illustrated Stadium. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. Retiring Reign midfielder Jess Fishlock called the field “atrocious.” Gotham defender Jess Carter was overheard saying the grounds were “so bad” when walking through the tunnel after the match. A week after Jaelin Howell injured her right ankle during a home game, the Gotham midfielder said the field was “pretty sandy” and “a little unstable.” Amorós acknowledged the rough conditions impacted the quality of the game. Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Corey Sipkin for the NY POST “At this level, in this kind of game, as a league, and we should have a better surface,” Amorós said. “Unfortunately, our club and football club did absolutely everything in their power to make sure that was the case. But luckily, it looks like nobody got hurt, and the game was what it was.” It’s not immediately clear if the NWSL penalized Gotham for a second consecutive week because of the field. item.title: NYCFC fires head coach Pascal Jansen after second-half collapse
item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. Getty Images The head coaching role will take on an even bigger role going into 2027 as NYCFC prepares for massive changes with the planned move into their new stadium and MLS changing their league calendar to a summer-through-spring format, which is in line with the European football calendar and includes an abbreviated sprint season that will run from February to May. The club views this next year as a “crucial point in franchise history” and the feeling is that NYCFC wants to make sure it has “the right leadership in place,” the source added. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
